newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pull back in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pull back in quiet session.

text.p: Argentine stocks gave back slim early gains and closed lower on light profit-taking Friday, with eyes set on next week's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve, dealers said.

"The market lacked volume today and some players grabbed profits ahead of the Fed talks, especially considering the pace always winds down for Yom Kippur," said Boston Securities trader Miguel Daneri of Monday's Jewish holiday.
The blue-chip MerVal index closed off 0.7 percent at 548, trimming the week's gains to 1.4 percent. The index stands 7.6 percent higher so far in September.

"The market has been growing steadily for weeks and needs to pause, as seen by foreign sell orders for Argentine stocks which are always triggered at certain levels such as 4.02 pesos for Telecom," said Daneri.
Floor volume slowed to 12.2 million pesos from Thursday's already very weak tally of 14.4 million, while over-the-counter deals totalled 70.1 million pesos compared to 81.5 million Thursday.
The dismal volumes could make the bolsa especially vulnerable to movements on Wall Street on the back of any unexpected decision by the Fed next Tuesday, dealers said.

A majority of Wall Street analysts expect the Fed to raise short-term rates to 5.5 percent from 5.25 percent to keep inflation at bay. The Fed's Open Market Committee will not meet again until after the U.S. presidential vote November 5.
The bolsa's broad market index shed 0.4 percent in the session, with losers outpacing winners 21 to 15 and 21 stocks closing unchanged.
Heaviest main-tier losses were in carmaker Sevel, sugar refiner Ledesma and foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata, which declined 3.1 percent, 2.5 percent and 2.1 percent, respectively.
Top performers were petrochemical concern Ipako, which rose 1.4 percent, and oil company Sol Petroleo and Bansud bank, both up 1.2 percent.
